_note: 40 needles, each stated exactly once in chapters ch1..ch3 (shape of adolion lab/needles). accept is a case-insensitive regex; answer is the key form, which appears exactly once in the transcript. asked marks the 30 questions (10 per chapter) asked as the player at c11; the other 10 are held back.

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The caravan master greets you at the paddock gate and gives her name as Odalys Venn before moving on down the line.
needles.question: What name did the caravan master give when she greeted us at the paddock gate?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: At the head of the line stands the lead camel, a scarred old bull the drovers call Brindlemoot.
needles.question: What do the drovers call the lead camel?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: Passage with the caravan costs eleven salt-coins, paid into a leather purse at the gate.
needles.question: How many salt-coins did passage with the caravan cost?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The night guard tells you the camp password is marrowfen, and warns you not to forget it.
needles.question: What was the camp password the night guard gave us?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The cook, a one-eyed man named Tobias Quell, ladles out lentils and grumbles about the heat.
needles.question: What was the one-eyed cook's family name?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The dune guide fingers his lucky charm, a small tortoise carved from green jade.
needles.question: What animal was the dune guide's lucky charm carved as?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The drovers name the coming sandstorm the Grey Widow and lash the loads down twice.
needles.question: What name did the drovers give the sandstorm?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: By morning the caravan's brass astrolabe is gone from the master's tent, stolen in the storm.
needles.question: What instrument was stolen from the master's tent during the storm?

needles.speaker: player
needles.statement: I stumble down the slip face and twist my left ankle badly, and I limp the rest of the day.
needles.question: Which part of me did I hurt on the slip face?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: You make camp in the lee of Saltjaw Dune, the tallest ridge for a day in any direction.
needles.question: Under which dune did we make camp?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The well-keeper will let you draw water only for a toll of a single blue feather.
needles.question: What toll did the well-keeper demand before we could draw water?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: A worn plaque names the place the Well of Ashkari, after a queen nobody remembers.
needles.question: What is the last well called?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: A rival caravan arrives flying a banner of a red scorpion and camps across the oasis.
needles.question: What creature was on the rival caravan's banner?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: Someone has scratched three words into the well stone: Mercy is salt.
needles.question: What three words were scratched into the well stone?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The gate sergeant is a heavy man called Hollis Durrant, and he reads every paper twice.
needles.question: What was the gate sergeant's family name?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: A flask of plum brandy changes hands, and the sergeant suddenly finds your papers in order.
needles.question: What did we bribe the gate sergeant with?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The city curfew bell rings at the hour of the owl, and after that the streets belong to the watch.
needles.question: At what hour does the Harrowgate curfew bell ring?

needles.speaker: player
needles.statement: I hand over forged papers that name me Merrit Callow, a salt factor from the coast.
needles.question: What false name did my forged papers give?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The quartermaster hides in plain sight behind a stall selling lacquered birdcages.
needles.question: What did the quartermaster's market stall sell?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: He introduces himself, very quietly, as Fenwick Sorrel, late of the border garrison.
needles.question: What was the quartermaster's family name?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: His maps of the river country cost forty crowns, and he will not haggle.
needles.question: How many crowns did the quartermaster want for his maps?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: Friendly doors in Harrowgate, he says, carry a small chalk spiral beside the latch.
needles.question: What chalk mark identifies friendly doors in Harrowgate?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: A pickpocket girl named Pim lifts your purse and then, laughing, hands it back.
needles.question: What was the pickpocket girl's name?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The magistrate is a thin, patient woman named Ysolde Marrick who never raises her voice.
needles.question: What was the magistrate's family name?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The charge read against you is smuggling indigo through the river gate.
needles.question: What were we charged with smuggling?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The witness who lied about you turns out to be the tanner's son from Mill Lane.
needles.question: Who was the witness that lied about us?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: Your sentence is lifted in exchange for an oath sworn on a silver thimble.
needles.question: What object was our oath sworn on?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The archive door grinds open only when you speak the word Selvane into the keyhole.
needles.question: What word opened the archive door?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: Your lanterns burn whale oil that smokes and stinks in the narrow stair.
needles.question: What did our lanterns burn in the archive stair?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: Carvings along the stair show a heron holding a key in its beak.
needles.question: What bird is carved along the archive stair?

needles.speaker: player
needles.statement: My brass compass slips from my belt and falls down the shaft, and I hear it hit water far below.
needles.question: What did I lose down the shaft?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The floodwater in the hall tastes of copper and stings the cuts on your hands.
needles.question: What did the floodwater in the hall taste of?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: A drowned statue rises from the water, and its plinth names it Queen Amarante.
needles.question: Whose drowned statue stands in the flooded hall?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: You cross the hall in a reed coracle found tied to a pillar.
needles.question: What kind of boat did we cross the flooded hall in?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: Pale eels the old archivists called glasstongues circle beneath the surface.
needles.question: What were the pale eels called?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: From a high shelf you recover the book you came for, the Ledger of Tides.
needles.question: What book did we recover from the flooded hall?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The keeper of the archive gives his name as Absalom, and says he has waited a long time.
needles.question: What name did the keeper of the archive give?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: His price for letting you leave is a lock of hair, cut with his own silver knife.
needles.question: What price did the keeper ask for letting us leave?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: He warns you never to sail under a red moon, or the archive will call you back.
needles.question: What did the keeper warn us never to sail under?

needles.speaker: narrator
needles.statement: The great tide, he says, will come at dawn of the seventh day.
needles.question: On which day did the keeper say the great tide would come?
